extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to the Spencer Foundation Small Research Grants on Education program (PIs with earned doctorates, affiliated with nonprofit/public institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the Spencer Foundation's Small Research Grants on Education program (projects up to $50,000, 1–5 years). Covers eligibility, proposal elements, budget rules, formatting limits, and optional supplemental course release materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Small Research Grants on Education Program supports education research projects that will contribute to the improvement of education, broadly conceived, with budgets up to $50,000 for projects ranging from one to five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-initiated: submissions are not in response to a specific request for topic, discipline, design, method, or location. Goal is to support rigorous, intellectually ambitious and technically sound research relevant to pressing questions and opportunities in education; scholarship that develops new foundational knowledge with lasting impact is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological and topical openness
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is open to multiple disciplinary and methodological perspectives and welcomes methodological diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed include quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, ethnographies, computational modeling, design-based research, participatory methods, and historical research. Projects may incorporate multiple data sources, span sufficient time for depth of understanding, and/or work closely with practitioners or community members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — focus on research about education
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be for research projects that aim to study education. Proposals for activities other than research are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ineligible activities include program evaluations with no significant research component, creation of professional development programs, curricula, assessment tools with no significant research component, scholarships, capital projects, and software development. Research focused on areas other than education is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI/Co-PI credential requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators (PIs) and Co-PIs must have an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or professional field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate students may be part of the team but may not be named the PI or Co-PI on the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational affiliation and administering organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must be affiliated with a non-profit organization or public/governmental institution willing to serve as the administering organization if the grant is awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include non-profit or public colleges, universities, school districts, research facilities, and other non-profits with 501(c)(3) status (or equivalent outside the U.S.). The Spencer Foundation does not award grants directly to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and currency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are accepted from the U.S. and internationally; all proposals must be submitted in English and budgets must be proposed in U.S. dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limit and indirect costs policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed budgets are limited to $50,000 total and may not include indirect cost charges per Spencer’s policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible investigators may also request supplemental funds for a course release (see optional supplemental course release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects proposed may not be longer than 5 years in duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI/Co-PI concurrency and submission restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may only hold one active research grant from the Spencer Foundation at a time and may not submit more than one research proposal to the Spencer Foundation at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction applies across Small Grants, Large Grants, Racial Equity Research Grants, and Research-Practice Partnership Program. Applicants with a proposal under consideration must wait for a final decision before submitting a new proposal. Exception: Spencer Vision Grants may be applied for even if there is another Spencer grant active or under review, but the Vision Grant project must be distinct from the other Spencer project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Personnel section requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the online application, indicate project personnel. The person creating the draft application is automatically assigned as PI; Co-PIs must follow portal steps before being added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also asked to confirm that neither the PI nor Co-PIs currently have another research proposal under review at Spencer (per Restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide project title, start and end dates, the central research question(s), and a 200-word project summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and budget justification structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget form is divided into categories (Salaries, Benefits, Other Collaborator, Travel, Equipment and Software, Project Expenses, Other, Subcontracts) and each expense should be added with a budget narrative describing that specific expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salaries choices include PI, Co-PI, Postdoc, Graduate Student, Undergraduate Researcher, etc. Benefits choices listed (PI Benefits, Tuition/Fees, Supplemental Course Release Benefits). Subcontracts require a separate subcontract budget form with the same categories. Detailed guidelines are available within the application form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Narrative content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a proposal narrative PDF that includes: a description of the project, the central research question(s), the project's significance; a rationale including literature summary, relationship to literature, expected contribution, and a summary of conceptual framework/theory; and a description of proposed research methods, participants, instruments, and modes of analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include information about sample/case definition and selection procedures; research design and context; description of key constructs, measures and data sources; procedures for data collection; and procedures for data analysis. The narrative may not exceed 1800 words and must include the word count in parentheses at its conclusion. References should follow the narrative in the same PDF and do not count toward the 1800-word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Narrative formatting and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative text should be double–spaced, in 12-point font, and may not exceed 1800 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables and figures can be included sparingly and do not count toward the word limit, but text in tables/figures will not count; however tables/figures must be described or explained in the narrative (which does count toward the word limit). Proposals exceeding the word limit will not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Timeline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a project timeline as a PDF indicating proposed start and end dates as well as key project events and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline may not exceed 1 page, text should be 12-point font. Major activities listed should be reflected in the proposal narrative. Proposed project duration can be up to 5 years. Teams should plan to begin timeline no sooner than 8 months from the original proposal submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Team document requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a PDF describing the project team that identifies roles, responsibilities and knowledge base of the PI, Co-PIs, and supporting researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Co-PIs and other supporting researchers are included, articulate how the team will work together and what each will contribute. May include a short description of the relationship between the team and the research site, if appropriate. This document should not exceed 250 words, be double–spaced in 12-point font, and will be reviewed along with the CVs of the PI and Co-PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Supplemental Course Release policy and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs or Co-PIs may request supplemental course release funds up to $10,000 over and above the $50,000 Small Grant limit (total up to $60,000) to support course release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible, the scholar must have a course load of 6 or above per academic year. Supplemental funds cannot be used for anything besides a course release and should be the standard rate at their institution. Only one additional course release per grant may be requested. Requesting supplemental funds does not guarantee they will be awarded. If a scholar's course load is less than 6, a course release may still be included but budget may not exceed $50,000 and requested documents are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials to apply for Supplemental Course Release
rubrics_metrics.description: Three additional application pieces are needed to request Supplemental Course Release funds: include the amount and a brief budget narrative in the Proposal Budget; upload a 250-word Course Release Rationale Statement; upload a Supporting Letter from the scholar's Dean or Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supporting Letter must: (a) confirm the scholar's course load is 6 courses or more per academic year, (b) confirm the scholar will be released from teaching a course if awarded the funds, and (c) confirm the budgeted amount for the course release is appropriate for their institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Agreement and Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be asked in the online portal to acknowledge that they have read, understood, and agree to comply with the Spencer Foundation's policy guidelines on the responsible and ethical use of generative AI technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the guidelines within the application portal for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission logistics and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are accepted two times per year and the online portal contains the full Request For Proposal and other applicant resources (optional appendices, review process, FAQs, writing guides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the portal (https://spencer.smartsimple.us/) for the full RFP, optional appendices, review process details, and other applicant resources.
